Daily card

Six words, two lines each, and it never scrolls. The guarantee is structural: the card is flex:1 in a fixed-height column and six flex:1 1 0 rows divide whatever it was given.

Six words

tacitadjunderstood without being said
brittleadjhard but easily broken
hedgeverbto avoid committing to one answer
lullnouna quiet interval in something noisy
quaintadjcharming in an old-fashioned way
rueverbto regret something bitterly

Worst case

circumlocutionarynessnouna way of speaking that goes all the way round the point before arriving at it, if it arrives at all
incomprehensibilitiesnounthings that cannot be understood however carefully they are explained
pellucidadj

Both lines are clamped to exactly one line — the term truncates, the definition truncates — and that is what makes the height predictable rather than hoped for. No term, no definition, no locale and no font substitution can change a row. The third row's meaning has not arrived yet and its placeholder sits inside the same line box, so the row does not resize.

Short card

tacitadjunderstood without being said
brittleadjhard but easily broken

Fewer than six is a real state, not an error. The rows spread out and the card keeps its shape. It is never padded with placeholder rows — six greyed slots would make a small collection feel like a failure.

No card yet

No card yet. Six words are waiting to be written out.

Nothing is generated until you press it.

The empty card occupies exactly the same slot in the budget as a made one, so pressing the button changes what is on the screen and never how the screen is arranged.
